name: Historic England National Heritage List search
fact: Historic England states the National Heritage List for England is the only official up-to-date register of nationally protected historic buildings and sites in England.
gate: Use the exact official list entry and legal designation; search/map discovery alone does not establish planning consent or impact acceptability.

name: NHLE search results and designation counts
fact: The official NHLE search exposes distinct categories including listed buildings, scheduled monuments, registered parks and gardens, protected wrecks, registered battlefields, World Heritage Sites, certificates of immunity and building preservation notices.
gate: Category presence/counts are national context, not parcel-level designation or consent evidence.

name: Historic England Open Data Hub listing downloads
fact: Historic England's Open Data Hub reports listed-building, scheduled-monument, park/garden, battlefield, protected-wreck and World Heritage Site GIS data updated 20 July 2026.
gate: Current GIS is authoritative screening evidence, but exact legal scope must still be checked against the official list entry/full-scale map and applicable law.

name: Understanding NHLE list entries
fact: Historic England explains that official list entries define legal designation scope and that quick-reference maps may not be to scale; older listed-building entries may use point/triangle mapping.
gate: Do not treat a map point or quick-reference polygon as exact curtilage/legal extent without reading the official entry and full-scale map.

name: What are scheduled monuments
fact: Scheduling protects nationally important archaeological sites and most works to a scheduled monument require Scheduled Monument Consent.
gate: Scheduled status is a separate statutory regime; planning permission, SMC and archaeological evaluation must not be collapsed into one state.

name: What are listed buildings
fact: Historic England defines listed buildings as buildings of special architectural or historic interest with legal protection through the NHLE.
gate: Listing does not by itself establish that a proposed change is acceptable, consented or outside curtilage.

name: What are registered parks and gardens
fact: Historic England's register identifies designed landscapes of special historic interest and records them on the NHLE.
gate: Registration is a planning heritage consideration, not a separate development consent or evidence that a particular proposal is acceptable.

name: What are registered battlefields
fact: Historic England identifies 47 registered battlefields and states there is no separate battlefield consent regime, while planning decisions give great weight to conservation.
gate: Registered battlefield overlap/proximity is not automatic refusal or approval; exact significance, archaeological potential and proposal effects require assessment.

name: What are protected wreck sites
fact: Historic England explains protected wreck sites are designated under the Protection of Wrecks Act 1973 and access/interference within restricted areas can require a licence.
gate: Protected-wreck designation/licensing is separate from terrestrial planning, marine licensing and other consents.

name: Apply for listing
fact: Historic England's listing application page, updated 13 July 2026, covers adding, amending or removing NHLE entries, Certificates of Immunity and Building Preservation Notices.
gate: An application, assessment or nomination is not a completed designation decision; use the current NHLE legal state.

name: Building Preservation Notices and Certificates of Immunity
fact: Historic England explains BPNs can temporarily protect a building for up to six months, while a granted Certificate of Immunity prevents listing/BPN for five years but does not prevent other designations.
gate: BPN and COI states are time-bounded and designation-specific; check exact start/end dates and other heritage controls.

name: Listed Building Consent
fact: Historic England states alterations, extensions or demolition affecting a listed building's special character may require Listed Building Consent from the local planning authority.
gate: Planning permission and Listed Building Consent are separate states; absence of one application record does not prove the other is unnecessary.

name: Scheduled Monument Consent
fact: Historic England's 26 May 2026 guidance states written Scheduled Monument Consent is required before most works to a scheduled monument and consent may carry pre-commencement conditions.
gate: Granted SMC does not substitute for planning permission, building regulations, ecological licences or compliance with SMC conditions.

name: Protected Wreck Sites planning consents
fact: Historic England explains designated wreck restricted areas and activities that require a Secretary of State licence, including diving/salvage directed at the wreck and damaging deposits.
gate: Wreck-site licence status must not be inferred from map presence, public access or marine project status.

name: Applying for protected wreck licences
fact: Historic England processes applications and advises the Secretary of State on protected-wreck access licences, which may be granted with conditions.
gate: Licence application/eligibility is not a granted licence; conditions and exact restricted-area activity remain material.

name: Heritage Consents index
fact: Historic England separates Listed Building Consent, planning permission, Scheduled Monument Consent, registered landscape/battlefield considerations, protected wreck licences and other heritage regimes.
gate: Do not infer one consent from another or merge statutory regimes into a single heritage status.

name: Planning Permission and historic environment
fact: Historic England explains that planning permission governs development and heritage impacts can be material, while Article 4 directions may remove permitted-development rights in some areas.
gate: Permitted-development assumptions require exact local controls; planning permission does not replace heritage-specific consent.

name: Decision-taking in the historic environment
fact: Historic England guidance emphasises proportionate understanding of heritage significance, appropriate expertise and assessment of proposal effects before planning/listed-building decisions.
gate: Designation alone is not an impact conclusion; decision evidence must address significance and the actual proposal.

name: Historic England planning system guidance
fact: Historic England's planning-system page, updated 8 May 2026, sets out legislation, national policy, decision making and Historic England's role in heritage planning.
gate: General policy context does not establish site-specific consent, consultation response or acceptable harm.

name: Historic England role in the planning system
fact: Historic England describes itself as the government's expert heritage adviser while statutory decision-makers remain responsible for balancing planning considerations.
gate: Historic England advice is not itself the final planning/LBC decision unless the relevant statutory regime expressly makes it so.

name: Support for listed property development
fact: Historic England recommends researching history, significance and condition and seeking early local-authority/pre-application advice before detailed redevelopment of historic buildings.
gate: Pre-application discussion or a heritage asset's reuse potential is not consent or proof of viability/deliverability.

name: Working with Historic England: heritage statements
fact: Historic England notes heritage statements may be required and should provide proportionate information sufficient to understand proposal impacts on significance.
gate: Submitting a heritage statement is not a finding of acceptable harm or an approved application.

name: Local Heritage Listing Advice Note 7
fact: Historic England Advice Note 7 third edition, published 15 May 2026, covers locally listed non-designated heritage assets and local-list preparation/review.
gate: Local listing is not statutory national designation; exact local policy weight and current adopted-list status must be checked.

name: Local Heritage Lists and Area Designations
fact: Historic England distinguishes local heritage lists and conservation areas from NHLE statutory listing/scheduling/registration and describes local management tools.
gate: Local list, conservation-area and national designation states must not be conflated; each has different legal/planning effects.
